subtitle: Quran revision, on schedule
promotionalText: Revise your hifz on a schedule that fits your life. Swipe through real mushaf pages, log every session, and see which pages are slipping before they're gone.
description:
Revisely is a Quran revision tracker built around a schedule that fits your hifz.

Pick how much you want to cover each day, and Revisely rotates through everything you've memorized on a repeating cycle. As you memorize more, the cycle grows with you. Miss a day and the schedule keeps moving instead of piling up, and when you're back, jump to any juz, surah or page.

Inside:

• Three ways to schedule: pages per day (1–60), juz per day (1–5), or a custom plan you build day by day, starting from any point
• Full-page mushaf revision: swipe through the actual pages of the Qur'an, check each one off, and optionally rate its strength from 1 to 5. A timer shows how long the session took
• Smart Tracking (optional): an Insights tab that ranks your memorized pages by how weak you've rated them and how often they've been skipped, so you know where to focus. Your daily assignment stays on schedule; this shows you what's slipping
• Fajr-aligned days: start your revision day at dawn instead of midnight, so a late-night session counts for the right day. Uses your location to calculate fajr
• Memorization manager: browse the Qur'an by surah, juz or hizb, and mark pages as you memorize them
• Daily log: a simple journal of what you memorized and revised each day, with your own notes
• Read tab and reading timer: a separate Qur'an reader for reading outside of revision, with timed reading sessions and your reading history
• Streaks, full session history with editing, and daily reminders

How it works:

1. Mark what you've already memorized
2. Choose how much to revise each day, and whether your day starts at fajr or midnight
3. Open the app each day, tap Start revision, and swipe through your pages

Sign in with Apple, Google or email, and your progress syncs across your devices. You can delete your account and all of its data at any time from Settings.

Built for people who want to keep the Qur'an they've memorized. Made to be used every day.
reviewNotes:
Revisely is a Quran revision tracker. It is free, with no in-app purchases.

The demo account is pre-populated so you land on a full dashboard: about 166 pages memorized (Al-Fatiha and the last six juz), some of Al-Baqarah in progress, and seven days of completed revision sessions ending yesterday, with Smart Tracking turned on.

New in 1.0.3:
- Prayer times: the compass icon at the top of Home opens the Prayer sheet (tabs Times and Qibla). Times asks for location the first time; Home then shows the next prayer under the header. Times are calculated on the device; the location is never sent to us. Settings > Prayer holds the times, calculation method, notifications and Qibla.
- Prayer notifications (Settings > Prayer > Prayer notifications), off until the user turns a prayer on: one at the prayer's time, an optional reminder 5–30 minutes before, standard tone or silent. Only the one at the prayer's time is Time Sensitive (the prayer's time is when it is needed); the reminder is an ordinary notification. They are scheduled on the device (no push server) and refreshed when the app opens.
- A Prayer times widget (Home Screen and Lock Screen): the next prayer and today's times; it opens the Prayer sheet. It joins Today, Verse of the day and Qibla (long-press the Home Screen > + > Revisely). Widgets get only what they show, through an App Group on the device.
- Home: the Today post says where today's revision starts ("Starts at Al-Hadid, p. 541"); its > opens Jump to (start today at another juz, surah or page) and Edit schedule. The "memorized" line opens Memorized pages.
- Fixes (the daily reminder no longer cancels the reading timer's notification).

Once signed in:
- Home shows today's revision. Tap "Start revision": the page fills the screen; tap it for the controls. Swiping past a page marks it revised (or tap the check at the top); ⋯ > Rate page strength rates it 1 to 5. Submit appears once every page is done, or swipe past the last page to finish.
- The bottom bar has three icon tabs: Home, Read (a separate Qur'an reader) and Insights (pages ranked by weakness and skips).
- The icons at the top right of Home open the Prayer sheet, Activity and Settings.
- In a session or the Read tab, the bottom bar holds Play, the reciter, Audio Options, the microphone (records the user reciting; View opens it in Activity) and the timer.
- Recitation (hold a verse > Play, or Play in the bar) continues with the app in the background or the phone locked, with Now Playing controls on the Lock Screen and a mini player in the app; this is what the audio background mode is for.
- Hold a verse > Translation: Saheeh International, or The Clear Quran® by Dr. Mustafa Khattab (⋯ > Select translation), from the publisher's API (Al-Furqaan Foundation) under their developer agreement.
- Settings > Support > Report a problem sends a short report (optionally a screenshot) to our error monitoring service.

Permissions:
- Microphone: only when the user taps record. Recordings stay on the device and are backed up to the user's own account (Wi-Fi only unless mobile data is allowed; Settings > Activity > Back up recordings turns it off). Only that account can read them; deleting a recording deletes its backup.
- Location: only when the user opens prayer times or the Qibla (used on the device only, never sent), or turns on Start day at fajr in Settings > Prayer (then saved to the account to calculate local fajr).
- Notifications: the daily revision reminder, the end of a timed session, and prayer notifications if the user turns them on.

Account deletion: Settings > Delete account (at the bottom) permanently deletes the account and all of its data, including backed-up recordings (guideline 5.1.1(v)).

Qur'an page images: the Madani Mushaf rendered with the King Fahd Complex fonts (open-source quran.com-images), served from our own storage.
